defects.detail: All 10 instances have P=3 and native_seconds H=3600. They render episode_seconds 648000 in instruction.md ('You have 648000 seconds'), task.toml [agent].timeout_sec=648000 and task.json guards. The specification's C7 formula is E = max(10800, ceil(10*W)) + 60*(P+1)*H. Its lower bound, independent of any measurement, is 10800 + 60*4*3600 = 874800. 648000 equals 60*P*H exactly, so the rendered E covers the full 60P allowance (180 serialized launches at the H guard) with zero time left for BPIPPRM calls or workflow overhead. The public_contract requires E to be 'derived by C7' and common to 10P/25P/60P. guards.json itself is labelled 'authoring defaults; C7 measurements must freeze these before release'. The published E therefore contradicts the authoritative contract formula. V = 21600 does satisfy max(21600, (P+1)*H+600).

The proposal's falsification sets an explicit kill threshold: mean excess cost must fall from the 10x to the 60x band by >=15 percentage points. C14 instead bootstraps the mean raw cost decrease in USD on pairs compliant at both endpoints, and says any positive 95% lower bound 'supports budget sensitivity'. That changes both the metric (raw dollars instead of excess cost over C_best) and the threshold (any nonzero decrease instead of 15 pp). A statistically detectable 1% improvement would therefore pass a falsifier the approved thesis would fail. This is the same kind of weakening that was just repaired for the C13/C14 near, far and match tolerances. baselines[7] restates that query-budget sensitivity is 'measured by C13-C14' and must stay consistent.
defects.suggested_remedy_text: In C14, measure the per-unit excess cost (C_panel-C_best)<path>:C_best at 10P and 60P on units with C_best>0. Require the mean decrease to be at least 0.15 (15 percentage points), using the existing bootstrap. Count failures as excess-cost-far, consistent with C13, rather than dropping them. Treat a smaller decrease as falsifying budget sensitivity. Mirror this criterion in baselines[7].

defects.detail: superposition30 may only pick from 3 sampled heights per source, while best400 refines to 0.01 m. Requiring it to match or beat best-known on at least 22 of 24 units can almost never fire even for fully additive scenarios. Meanwhile, the proposal's toy agent beat the reference by searching 1-m combinations and refining to 0.01 m. The nonadditivity hypothesis is therefore effectively unfalsifiable.
defects.suggested_remedy_text: Let superposition30 refine heights continuously between sampled responses (or use finer per-source height grids within 30P), and define 'matching' as within a declared per-unit tolerance of best-known cost.

defects.detail: The proposal selects on admissible, n_sources 2..6, n_binding_standards >= 1 and the Tier 3 >= 70% quota, the last because ARM2 units were solved exactly. These predicates then become release-blocking checks, and acceptance_criteria[3] says they 'cannot be repaired by invented selectors'. Allow the Tier 3 >= 70% and downwash >= 30% quotas to be met by narrowing the selection on those real catalog attributes (adjusting count and min_units together), rather than declaring any selector repair forbidden.

defects.component: bind renderer (draft template height spelling) + tests/grade.py bpip_input/cases height representability check
defects.detail: grade.py cases() (SRCPARAM j==4) and bpip_input() take the allowed height precision from the draft's spelled value, precision = -exponent of the template field, and reject any design height not representable at that precision with E_DESIGN_MISMATCH. The draft heights are str(float) of height_max_m, so trailing zeros are dropped. Units with gep 65.0 or 81.3 end up with 1-dp height fields, while the published height_min_m values have 2 dp. Reproduced from the snapshot: 04ef47cb1279 (field '65.0', 1 dp; mins 8.04, 11.43, 9.51, 8.72, 14.45, 8.47), 074897d0f159 ('65.0'; 15.71, 11.43), 4ef687ff4418 ('65.0'; 12.97, 13.05) and 0558a6a6c25d ('81.3'; 18.43, 15.42). None of these minimums is representable at 1 dp. A design.yaml with stack_height_m equal to the published height_min_m therefore passes design() (lo <= h <= hi) but is rejected E_DESIGN_MISMATCH in bpip_input ('BPIP design height 8.04 is not representable at 1 decimal places'). instruction.md tells the student to choose 'a height within its closed physical bounds' and prices extension from height_min_m, so the stated cost-zero stack is unwinnable on 4 of 10 pilot units. On the other 6 units (fields such as '82.27') it is legal. Height resolution and the reachable optimum therefore differ between units for a reason unrelated to the scenario. This also contradicts the spec's comparator definitions (coordinate40/best400 step 0.01 m and superposition30 'height resolution is 0.01 m'): those candidates would be rejected on these units. Required correction: make the height-field precision uniform and at least as fine as the published bounds' precision for every unit, then re-render task.json, drafts and instructions consistently.
